mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day S&P 500 return following months with FEDFUNDS < 2.5% is negative over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when UNRATE rises >0.3pp over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicate robust consumer demand and economic momentum, generating multiplicative positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: The average 60-day SPX return when both HOUST and RSAFS are above 3-month moving averages is negative over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening supply chain activity during high-inflation regimes, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high-inflation regimes, the average 20-day SPX return following INDPRO < 12-month moving average is positive over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI (CPIAUCSL) reading above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average indicates sustained consumer confidence and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 5-day SPX return following months with HOUST > 12-month moving average is negative over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase below 100,000 signals labor market weakness that constrains consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when PAYEMS < 100,000 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average indicates robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day SPX return following months with INDPRO > 12-month moving average is negative over a 5-year rolling window.
